notes: Contraction of people-replace-0001 on spouse_of (functional and symmetric): removes the revision's original fact, 'Marie Curie's husband was Pierre Curie'. Direct, paraphrase, cross-lingual and the revision's far question (nationality of her husband, stored about Pierre by name) are reused from the revision. Near uses symmetry. Cardinality question: Henri Becquerel, who is tied to the Curies by the 1903 prize but was not married to Marie; the revision's new object Winston Churchill was dropped because his wife Clementine is a separately stored fact that rules him out whatever happens to Marie's marriage. The two 2-hop derived questions go through the removed fact (a description: the first woman to win a Nobel Prize; and 'her husband' followed by his birthplace). The revision's questions about her husband being a prime minister or a literature laureate were dropped (their original answer 'no' is the same kind of question as the cardinality one) and its premise question about the 1903 prize is world-dependent (Hase et al.), so not used here.
